regional-governor.ts:
Ensure the named card cannot be played by any opponent of Regional Governor's player (all 2-3 of them).
Ensure an eliminated player is not affected (they are no longer a player).
Ensure that if another player takes control of Regional Governor, the restriction still applies to the original player's opponents (effect is not changed).
regional-governor.a2:
Ensure the named card cannot be played by either enemy player.
Ensure the named card can be played by the friendly teammate.

relentless#konstantines-folly.ts:
Ensure the first event played by each opponent each round loses all abilities, tracked separately per opponent (opponent B's first event is affected even if opponent A already played one).
Ensure an opponent's second and later events that round are unaffected, and that the tracking resets next round.
relentless#konstantines-folly.a2:
Ensure the first event played by each enemy player each round loses all abilities, tracked separately per enemy.
Ensure the friendly teammate's events are never affected.

admiral-ozzel#overconfident.ts:

Ensure both enemy players may ready a unit.
Ensure the friendly teammate is not offered the choice (not an opponent) and the played Imperial unit comes from your own hand only.

k2so#cassians-counterpart.ts:

k2so#cassians-counterpart.a2:
Ensure the When Defeated choice is made separately for each of the two enemy players, and the teammate is not affected.
Ensure Overwhelm excess damage goes to the base of whichever enemy controls the attacked unit.

saw-gerrera#extremist.ts:

agent.q: May the controller attack with a readied friendly Wookiee that belongs to the teammate?
agent.a: No. Players may not attack with their teammate's units; an attack is never initiated with a teammate's unit. The teammate's unit can still be chosen and readied (friendly includes the teammate); only the 'attack with it' part cannot be done (do as much as possible). The 'Always Two: Rules Unknown' tag can be dropped.

agent.q: Do units of eliminated players still count for 'only player who controls units in that arena' (draft line 2)?
agent.a: No. An eliminated player's owned cards are removed and cards owned by others in their play area go to their owners' discard piles, so they control no units; they are not players for effects. Draft line is correct but just restates elimination.
agent.c: CR v9.0 11.3.1, 11.3.2; format-rules Twin Suns table ('Eliminated players: not players for any effect')

agent.q: Does a unit controlled by your teammate in that arena stop you being 'the only player who controls units' there?
agent.a: Yes, by the text. A teammate is another player in the game, and 'only player who controls units' counts players, so the teammate controlling a unit there means you are not the only player (control is personal; the teammate controlling it is not 'you'). Derived from the text and the Doubles definition, not an explicit card ruling. If you win via the card, both teammates win.
agent.c: Doubles overview ('A teammate is another player in the game'; 'If one teammate wins the game via a card ability, they both win'); format R6, R11
agent.s: Ensure the win does not trigger if the teammate controls a unit in the chosen arena, even when no enemy does.

agent.q: 'Play only as your first action in the action phase': with one shared action per team turn, is it the player's own first action or the team's first action (if the teammate already took the team's first action)?
agent.a: UNSETTLED. Turns and actions are shared by the team, while 'you' is personal; no rule says which reading applies to 'your first action'. The official ruling only says it must be played by the Play a Card action as the first action.

agent.q: Upgrade can be played on any unit, including a unit another player controls. Who assigns the indirect damage then?
agent.a: 'You' in the granted ability is the controller of the attached unit, so when the unit is controlled by another player (an opponent's in Twin Suns, the teammate's or an enemy's in Always Two), that unit's controller assigns the indirect damage it deals, not the player who played the upgrade. The upgrade's controller stays the player who played it.
agent.c: CR v9.0 1.2.f ('If that upgrade gives abilities to the attached unit, the unit's controller resolves those abilities'); R20; R34
agent.s: Ensure when attached to a unit another player controls, that unit's controller assigns all indirect damage the unit deals, not the player who played the upgrade.

agent.q: In what order do the players choose which unit to return?
agent.a: Starting with the active player, clockwise; all returns finish before the defeat-all. In Always Two the teammate is a player and chooses too (seating per R8). Each player may decline.
agent.c: Official ruling on Rhydonium Detonation ('Starting with the active player, each player chooses a unit to return...'); R9; R11
agent.s: Ensure each player in turn, starting with the active player and going clockwise, may return a non-leader unit (in Always Two the teammate chooses too), and the defeat-all happens only after every choice is resolved.

agent.q: Who chooses, in what order, and can a player pick a unit they do not control?
agent.a: Each player (Always Two: teammate included) chooses one unit they control themselves; choices are made in turn clockwise starting with the player who played the card (the card gives no other start). Chosen units are then defeated; the shuttle itself may be chosen by its controller. Eliminated players are not players.
agent.c: R9; R11; card text 'chooses a unit they control'; CR v9.0 Twin Suns 12.4.2 context (eliminated players are not players, per format-rules Twin Suns table)
agent.s: Ensure each player (Always Two: teammate included) chooses a unit they themselves control, in turn clockwise from the player who played the card, and all chosen units are defeated.

agent.q: Followup card with no draft lines: how does the extra regroup phase work with several players and Max Rebos?
agent.a: The additional regroup phase is a full regroup (every player draws 2, resources a card, readies), and each Max Rebo in play causes its own additional phase, whoever controls it (a teammate's or an opponent's counts). In Twin Suns the game ends at the end of the phase in which a player is eliminated, so an elimination during the first regroup ends the game before the additional one.
